# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a Path tab (native path trace, native Linux and WSL2 only: on macOS, Windows and WSL1 `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row prefills it; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

6	## The container engine — `internal/engine` and `internal/docker`
7	
8	**`internal/engine`** names the engine in use — docker or podman — and carries
9	everything that is not the same between the two: the binary, the credential
10	helper prefix, the auth file, the host socket, and the `--format` templates. It
11	is its own package rather than a field of `internal/docker` because
12	`internal/scan` needs the same answer and does not import `internal/docker` —
13	`internal/forge`'s arrangement read one level down (§3.67).
14	
15	`engine.Resolve(preference)` turns `app.container_engine` into a `Shape`:
16	`auto` takes docker if it is on PATH and podman otherwise; a pinned engine that
17	is absent is an **error**, never the other one, because the two do not hold the
18	same containers. Anything else is taken as a path to a binary. The router
19	resolves once at startup and once per context switch, into `engine.SetCurrent`.
20	
21	A `Shape` carries **no resolved filesystem path**: `AuthPaths()`, `AuthPath()`
22	and `HostSocket()` are methods. The shape is built at package initialisation, so
23	a `$HOME` read there would be frozen before anything else runs — and whether the
24	socket exists is the whole question, since `podman system service` can start or
25	stop while the application is up.
26	
27	**`internal/docker`** drives that engine. Every invocation goes through one
28	seam — `dockerRunner`, implemented by `cliRunner` (`exec.go`) — which is what
29	made podman cheap: the binary name lived in exactly one place. The package is
30	split by resource: `containers.go`, `images.go`, `networks.go`, `volumes.go`,
31	`registry.go`, `system.go`, `launch.go`, plus `exec.go` (the seam), `parse.go`,
32	`container_ports.go`, `identifier.go` and `names.go`. It is **not** called
33	`internal/container`: renaming it would touch 40 files for a vocabulary gain.
34	
35	Two things about the engine are worth knowing before changing this code:
36	
37	- **The `--format` templates are per engine and identical today.** Podman
38	  implements `--format`, but equality of the *fields* is guaranteed nowhere, and
39	  a divergence raises no error — it produces wrong rows. No measurement has been
40	  taken against a real podman; `TestTheTwoTemplateSetsAreStillUnmeasured` fails
41	  the day the two sets stop matching, so a divergence is recorded deliberately.
42	- **`system df -v` is scraped, not templated**, and is therefore disabled under
43	  podman (`Shape.ParsesSystemDFVerbose`). It is a fixed-width table read at
44	  offsets taken from its header line, and there is no `--format` that exposes
45	  per-image unique size.
46	
47	- **Four typed, read-only reads for the Path tab** (`container_network.go`,
48	  DEVDESK-330, DEVDESK-331), each with a `context.Context` that kills the
49	  invocation: `InspectContainerNetworking(ctx, id)`, `ListContainersContext(ctx,
50	  all)` (`ListContainers(all)` is unchanged and does not use it),
51	  `EngineOperatingSystem(ctx)` and `InspectNetworkBridge(ctx, networkID)`. They
52	  run `container inspect`, `ps`, `info` and `network inspect` and nothing else. `InspectContainerNetworking` runs
53	  `container inspect --format <containerNetworkingFormat> <id>`: the format
54	  selects `Name`, `HostConfig.NetworkMode`, `State.Running` and, per network,
55	  `NetworkID` (`EndpointNetwork.NetworkID`, kept only when it passes
56	  `IsContainerID`, else empty), `IPAddress`, `Gateway` and `GwPriority`, so `Config.Env`, labels and mounts are
57	  never read into memory. It reads stdout only, and its error carries the
58	  command label, never the output. The ID must pass `IsContainerID` and is one
59	  argv element, never a name. The inspect and `info` reads refuse a non-Docker
60	  engine with `ErrDockerOnly` before any invocation; output over 256 KiB
61	  (`maxInspectBytes`) is refused. `InspectContainer`, which returns the whole
62	  `docker inspect` JSON (secrets included) with stdout and stderr merged and no
63	  context, was not reused for that reason. The `info` format
64	  (`{{.OperatingSystem}}`) is a docker-only literal and is not in
65	  `engine.Templates`.
66	- `internal/docker/netdiag.go` — **gone**. §3.33 took the five probes that did not need a container, §3.43 the ports table, §3.44 the topology (and with it `docker/topology.go` and the last `--privileged`), §3.47 the route trace and the file itself (the trace came back in the process as `internal/nettrace`, DEVDESK-327). §3.61 removed the OCI connectivity test, and with it the last container this application runs for a diagnostic: `networks.go` now holds only `ListNetworks`, `CreateNetwork`, `RemoveNetwork`, `PruneNetworks` and `InspectNetwork`.
67	
68	## OCI registries — `internal/oci`
69	
70	`internal/oci/oci.go` — an OCI **registry** HTTP client: list tags,
71	download and extract a tar.gz (a repository template is one — `templates.md`). It speaks the distribution spec over `net/http`
72	and never shells out, so it is engine-agnostic and podman changed nothing in it.
73	
74	**Typed status errors and context variants (DEVDESK-298, IS-18).** A registry
75	or token endpoint answering with a non-success status returns
76	`*oci.StatusError{Code, Source, Challenge}`; read it with `errors.As`. `Source`
77	is `SourceRegistry` (the v2 API) or `SourceToken` (the Bearer token endpoint).
78	`Challenge` is the `Www-Authenticate` header of a 401 whose challenge is not
79	Bearer. `Error()` keeps the three historical messages to the character
80	(`registry returned 404`, `token endpoint returned 403`,
81	`unexpected auth challenge: ...`), so nothing on screen or in a log changed.
82	Failures that are not a status (unreadable body, missing realm, no token
83	field) stay plain errors and do not match `errors.As`.
84	
85	The unexported `unexpectedChallenge` field is a deviation from the plan, which
86	had only `Code`, `Source` and `Challenge`: with those three, a 401 with a
87	non-Bearer challenge and a 401 returned by the registry after a token exchange
88	both read `Source == SourceRegistry`, `Code == 401`, and `Error()` could not
89	give each its own message. The flag tells them apart without widening the
90	exported surface.
91	
92	`ListRegistryTagsContext` and the `...Context` variants of `registryGET`,
93	`registryDo`, `doRequest` and `exchangeBearerToken` take a `context.Context`
94	(the token endpoint request included) and check `ctx.Err()` at the head of
95	every page. The old names delegate with `context.Background()`, signatures
96	unchanged. A deadline or a cancel reaches the caller as an error that
97	satisfies `errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)` or `context.Canceled`,
98	and never as a `StatusError`. **Limit:** `registryHTTPClient` keeps its own
99	`Timeout: 15s` per request, and the client wraps `context.DeadlineExceeded`
100	for that timeout too. A caller cannot tell the client timeout from the
101	context's deadline, so `imagesearch.Classify` (DEVDESK-303, IS-12) puts both in
102	the `failed` verdict.
103	
104	**Credentials stay on their origin (DEVDESK-410).** Three guards keep the Basic
105	credentials and the Bearer token from leaving the registry they were meant for:
106	
107	- **The tag list never follows a `Link: rel="next"` to another origin.**
108	  `ListRegistryTagsContext` checks each `next` with `sameOrigin` (the catalog
109	  walker's guard) before the next request. A foreign `next` is an error that
110	  wraps `ErrTagsNextOffOrigin` (test it with `errors.Is`) and names the
111	  destination host only. No partial list is returned: a short list could pass
112	  for the whole one, and `imageupdate` and the security remediation would read
113	  a false "up to date". The catalog walker behaves otherwise: it returns
114	  `truncated=true` with the names already read, and no error.
115	- **`registryHTTPClient` has a `CheckRedirect`, `refuseOffOriginRedirect`.** A
116	  redirect is refused when its scheme, host or port differ from the first
117	  request of the chain (`via[0]`, not only the previous hop), so a chain that
118	  leaves the origin and comes back is refused too. The error reads
119	  `refusing redirect to another origin (<host>)` and wraps
120	  `errOffOriginRedirect` (`errors.Is`). It holds neither the target URL, nor
121	  its path or query: `redirectRefusal` strips the `*url.Error` that carries
122	  them, so a signed URL reaches neither the footer nor the logs. The limit of 10 redirects (`maxRedirects`, the `net/http` default) is
123	  kept. It applies to everything that uses the client: tags, catalog and the
124	  token endpoint.
125	- **The token endpoint's answer is capped at 1 MiB** (`maxTokenResponse`). A
126	  larger body is an error (`token response over 1048576 bytes`), not a silent
127	  cut.
128	
129	**Behavior change.** Some redirects that were followed are now refused: `http`
130	to `https` on the same host, `host` to `host:443`, and a host written with a
131	different case. The comparison is on the exact scheme and `host:port`, and the
132	guard refuses when in doubt.
133	
134	**Catalog walk (DEVDESK-306, IS-03).** `ListCatalogContext(ctx, apiURL,
135	username, password, maxPages, pageSize)` returns `(names, truncated, err)`. It
136	asks `<apiURL>/v2/_catalog?n=<pageSize>` and follows `Link: rel="next"` for at
137	most `maxPages` pages (non-positive limits are an error). `truncated` is true
138	when names were left: the page cap was reached with a `next` link, more than
139	`maxPages*pageSize` names came back (the list is cut to that), or the `next`
140	link points to another origin. Each page body is capped at 1 MiB; a larger
141	page is an error, not a silent cut. A non-200 answer is a `*StatusError`.
142	Authentication is the tags' flow: Basic, then Bearer on a challenge, the token
143	kept across pages.
144	
145	- **`next` is followed only to the same origin.** `sameOrigin` compares scheme
146	  and host strictly (`host` and `host:443` differ), so a registry cannot make
147	  the walk send the Basic credentials or the token elsewhere. A foreign or
148	  differently written `next` ends the walk as `truncated`, with no error.
149	- **HTTP 3xx redirects are hardened too** (DEVDESK-410): the walk goes through
150	  `registryHTTPClient`, whose `CheckRedirect` refuses a redirect to another
151	  origin (see "Credentials stay on their origin" above).
152	
153	## Image search — `internal/imagesearch` (DEVDESK-298, IS-18)
154	
155	Pure Go, no UI. Types and one interface; two adapters, `HubSearcher` (IS-02)
156	and `CatalogSearcher` (IS-03); dhi.io is IS-17:
157	
158	- `Target`: one registry to search (`EntryKey`, `Alias`, `RegistryURL`,
159	  `APIURL`, `RepoPrefix`, `Username`, `Password`; the credentials are empty for
160	  an anonymous entry, D12).
161	- `Query{Text, Limit}`: `Limit` 0 is the adapter's default.
162	- `Image`: one result (`EntryKey`, `Name`, `Repo`, `Description`, `Stars`,
163	  `HasStars`, `Official`). `Repo` is the final path, with the prefix and
164	  `library/` applied once (D39).
165	- `Searcher.Search(ctx, Target, Query) (images, partial, err)`, and
166	  `SearcherFunc`, the function adapter.
167	- `HubSearcher` (DEVDESK-301, IS-02, `hub.go`): anonymous, one GET on
168	  `https://index.docker.io/v1/search` (the endpoint `docker search` uses, not a
169	  public Hub contract), one page of at most `HubLimit` (50) results, no
170	  credentials (Target's are ignored), no redirects, 15 s client timeout, body
171	  capped at 1 MiB. A non-200 answer is an `*oci.StatusError`. A result without
172	  `star_count` keeps `HasStars` false (the Stars cell stays empty, never 0).
173	  Names are validated against a regex (`hubComponent`: lowercase alphanumerics
174	  joined by `.`, `_`, `__` or runs of `-`, as in the OCI distribution spec); a
175	  name that fails is dropped (`-rm`, `--help`, uppercase, `a//b`, a leading or
176	  trailing separator). A description is sanitised: escape sequences, control
177	  characters and Unicode format characters (category Cf: bidi overrides,
178	  zero-width, BOM) are removed. Privacy: the text the user typed is sent to
179	  Docker Hub as soon as a Hub entry is checked.
180	- `ByRegistry(hub, other)` (`route.go`): a target whose host is exactly `dhi.io`
181	  (DEVDESK-303, `isDHI`: case, scheme, port and path ignored; `registry.dhi.io`
182	  and `notdhi.io` are not dhi.io) is refused first, with `ErrUnsupported` and no
183	  request to either searcher, since dhi.io has no documented catalogue API
184	  (IS-17). Otherwise a target for which `oci.IsDockerHub(RegistryURL)` is true
185	  goes to `hub`, any other to `other`. A nil searcher answers `ErrUnsupported`
186	  with no request at all. Production uses
187	  `ByRegistry(HubSearcher{}, CatalogSearcher{})`: Hub goes to the Hub search,
188	  every other registry to its catalog. `isDHI` parses the URL (`url.Parse`, with
189	  `https://` added when there is no scheme) and compares `Hostname()`, so
190	  userinfo (`dhi.io@evil.example`), a trailing dot and a port cannot fool it.
191	- `CatalogSearcher` (DEVDESK-306, IS-03, `catalog.go`): searches a private
192	  registry by walking `/v2/_catalog` through `oci.ListCatalogContext` and
193	  filtering **client-side**: the text the user typed is never sent to the
194	  registry. Steps, in order:
195	  1. The query is trimmed; fewer than `CatalogMinQueryRunes` (2) runes returns
196	     `ErrQueryTooShort` with **no request**.
197	  2. The walk: `CatalogPageSize` (1000) names per page, at most
198	     `CatalogMaxPages` (10) pages, so at most 10 000 names. A cut walk sets
199	     `truncated`. An error from the walk (status, deadline, unreadable page)
200	     is returned as is, with no row.
201	  3. Guard R1 (before the filter): when the target has a `RepoPrefix`, only the
202	     names that start with `<prefix>/` are candidates. If the walk is complete and
203	     no name carries the prefix, the answer is `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` (the
204	     cause names the prefix); this protects against a catalog that does not
205	     list names the way the entry reaches them (Nexus, IS-16) and would
206	     otherwise read as a false "no result". If the walk is truncated, the
207	     prefix may be on a page not read: the answer is no result with
208	     `partial` set, not an error.
209	  4. Filter: case-insensitive substring match on the part **after** the prefix.
210	     `Image.Name` is that part, `Image.Repo` the full catalog name.
211	  5. Only valid names are kept (`validRepoPath`, `names.go`: every
212	     `/`-separated component follows the distribution-spec grammar, as for Hub);
213	     others are dropped.
214	  6. Order by `MatchTier`, then name, then `Repo`; at most `CatalogMaxRows`
215	     (100) rows (`Query.Limit` can only lower that). Rows cut by the limit set
216	     `partial`, as does a truncated walk.
217	
218	  `MatchTier` (ranks 0 to 4, see the order below) now lives in `imagesearch`
219	  (`names.go`) so the searcher and the table share one ranking;
220	  `oci_resources.matchTier` delegates to it. The 15 s per-registry deadline
221	  (`imageSearchDeadline`, below) covers the whole walk; hitting it is a
222	  `failed` verdict with no row. `CatalogSearcher.List` replaces
223	  `oci.ListCatalogContext` in tests. Walks per search
224	  (DEVDESK-311, IS-07, `walks.go`): `WithSharedWalks(ctx)` puts a memo on the
225	  batch context and `CatalogSearcher` goes through `walkCatalog`, so a search
226	  queries `/v2/_catalog` once per API URL and identity. Without the memo
227	  (any other caller) every call walks on its own.
228	  - Key: the exact API URL (trailing slash ignored) and the identity, an
229	    HMAC-SHA256 of username and password under a random per-batch key: no
230	    secret is held in clear and the key prints no userinfo. Two identities
231	    never share a walk, because Harbor, Artifactory and GitLab filter the
232	    catalog per account. A `credentials` entry with no effective secret shares
233	    the walk of an anonymous entry. A member on another port or subdomain has
234	    another API URL and is not grouped.
235	  - Leader and followers: the first call for a key walks, the others wait (or
236	    return on their own context). It is a memo, not a singleflight: the key is
237	    kept after the walk, so a member arriving later reuses the result, and it
238	    dies with the batch (no cache between two searches).
239	  - A shared failure (a 503, say) is the same error for every member, so the
240	    same verdict (`failed` or `refused`), one message per entry. A result
241	    caused by the leader's own context ending is not memoized: followers
242	    already waiting on that flight receive the leader's context error (verdict
243	    `failed`), and only members arriving afterwards walk again. A
244	    panic in the leader gives followers a sentinel error (`errWalkAborted`),
245	    never an empty catalog.
246	  - `repo_prefix` filtering, `partial`, `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` and
247	    `Cached only` stay computed per member.
248	  - Unverified assumption: members of one host answer on the same
249	    `/v2/_catalog` (IS-16).
250	  A catalog may be disabled or filtered to the account's rights (Harbor,
251	  Artifactory, GitLab): the answer is then `refused` or a shortened list.
252	- **Verdicts (DEVDESK-303, IS-12, `verdict.go`).** `Classify(err, n, partial)`
253	  is a pure function that turns one registry's answer into an `Outcome{Verdict,
254	  Partial, Skipped}`. `Verdict` is one of `VerdictOK` (`ok`), `VerdictNoResult`
255	  (`no result`), `VerdictRefused` (`unsupported or refused`) and
256	  `VerdictFailed` (`failed`); the zero value is not a verdict (`pending`) and
257	  `Classify` never returns it. `Partial` and `Skipped` are marks, not verdicts:
258	  `Partial` with `ok` or `no result` (invariant Q1: a walk cut short that found
259	  nothing is still `no result`, marked `Partial`), never with `refused` or
260	  `failed`, never with `Skipped`; `Skipped` only with `no result`. Rules, first
261	  match wins:
262	  1. no error: `n > 0` is `ok`, `n == 0` is `no result`; `Partial` is kept as
263	     given in both cases;
264	  2. `ErrQueryTooShort` is `no result` with `Skipped`;
265	  3. `ErrUnsupported` or `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` is `refused`;
266	  4. a `*oci.StatusError` is `refused` when `refusedStatus` holds: 401 and 403
267	     from either source, 404 and 405 from `SourceRegistry` only (a 404 from the
268	     token endpoint is a failure); any other status, 429 and 5xx included, is
269	     `failed`;
270	  5. anything else is `failed`: deadline, cancel, network, unreadable or
271	     oversized body, invalid request.
272	
273	  `ErrQueryTooShort` and `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` are returned by
274	  `CatalogSearcher` (DEVDESK-306).

276	## Image updates — `internal/imageupdate` (§3.88)
277	
278	Three tables carry an **Update** column (`internal/ui/updatecol`): oci's Images
279	tab, the containers list, and the Remediation tab of a scan result. It shows an
280	arrow when the image's registry holds something newer, and says what:
281	
282	| Kind | When | Cell |
283	|---|---|---|
284	| `NewPatch` | the tag has ≥ 3 version components and a tag differing only by the last, same variant, is higher (`20.11.1-alpine` → `20.11.4-alpine`) | the arrow and the tag |
285	| `NewBuild` | the digest the tag points to now is none of the local image's digests | the arrow alone (`IconArrowDown`) |
286	
287	A newer patch wins over a new build. Every other state says why there is no
288	arrow, in grey — a blank used to stand for all of them, which in the
289	Remediation tab (bases rarely pinned, often not held locally) meant a column
290	that was silent without saying why:
291	
292	| Kind | Cell | When |
293	|---|---|---|
294	| `UpToDate` | the check mark | the local digest is the tag's |
295	| `Pending` | `IconHourglass` | no answer yet |
296	| `Failed` | `IconHelpCircle` | the registry did not answer (logged) |
297	| `LocalBuild` | `IconHammer` | images, containers: no registry digest |
298	| `NotLocal` | `IconCloud` | Remediation: unpinned, and not held by the engine |
299	| `Pinned` | `IconPin` | a digest with no tag: nothing can move |
300	| `None` | blank | the question does not apply (untagged image, unresolved `FROM`) |
301	
302	Every state but a newer patch is one glyph (`updatecol.Cell`): the words cost
303	eleven cells in the widest table there is, and the reason is still spelled out
304	by `G`'s greyed shortcut in the footer and by `?`. `Status.Label` keeps the
305	word, which is what the filter matches. `Evaluate` takes what "no local digest"
306	means to its caller (`LocalBuild` or `NotLocal`). The column's filter only matches an update's label, or `/ca`
307	would find every `local build`. A tag with fewer components (`3.20`,
308	`20`) has no patches of its own — it floats over them, so a new patch moves the
309	tag and the digest says it. That is also the only answer a floating tag
310	(§3.79) ever gets.
311	
312	**The registry's side is cached, the comparison is not.** `imageupdate.Check`
313	keeps, per reference, the tag's digest and the newer patch tag in
314	`~/.devdesk/cache/image-updates.json` — 6 hours for an answer, 30 minutes for a
315	failure (unknown repository, no credentials) so it is not asked on every
316	refresh. `Evaluate` compares with the local digests each time a row is built,
317	so a pull clears the arrow without asking the registry again.
318	
319	**Two requests at most per reference.** The digest is a `HEAD` on the manifest
320	(`oci.ManifestDigest`) accepting an OCI index and a Docker manifest list — a
321	multi-platform tag's digest is the index's, the one `docker pull` records in
322	`RepoDigests`. Docker Hub does not count a `HEAD` against its pull rate limit.
323	The tag list (`oci.ListRegistryTags`) is only read for a tag with a patch
324	component. At most four references are asked at once; credentials are the
325	engine's (`docker.GetStoredCreds`), as for the Remediation tab.
326	
327	**What each view compares with:**
328	
329	- *Images* — the image's own `RepoDigests`, now read by the same `image
330	  inspect` that reads its size (`templates().ImageInspect`). Only a tagged image
331	  **with** a digest is asked about: one built or loaded here has none, and its
332	  name would send the question to a registry that never heard of it.
333	- *Containers* — the digests of the image the container was **created from**
334	  (`docker.ContainerImageDigests`: `container inspect` for the image ID, then
335	  `image inspect`). After a pull the container still runs the old image, so the
336	  arrow stays until it is recreated — which is what it is there to say. The
337	  digests are read again only when the set of containers changes, not on every
338	  two-second refresh.
339	- *Remediation* — the digest the Dockerfile pins, or else the image the engine
340	  holds under that name (`docker.ImageRepoDigests`). A base the engine does not
341	  hold only gets the patch side.
342	
343	`imageupdate.Tracker` is what each view keeps between checks: the facts it has
344	and the references a check is out for, so a reload asks only what is new or
345	stale. Every view reaches the network through a package variable its tests
346	replace.
347	
348	**Updating — `G` on the Images tab.** It pulls what the column points at (the
349	newer patch tag, or the same tag again for a new build) and removes the image
350	it replaces, by ID and never forced. It refuses while any container, running
351	or stopped, was created from that image (`docker.ContainersUsingImage`, `ps -a
352	--filter ancestor=`): removing it would break the container, and keeping it
353	would leave the update half done. The check is made twice — from the engine's
354	container count to grey `G` (Rule 130; docker only, podman reports none), and
355	against the engine just before the pull, since a container can appear in
356	between. A pull that brings the image already held removes nothing
357	(`docker.SameImageID`). It runs as a pull job, so the row spins and `K` stops
358	it; every refusal and failure is a footer line naming why (the containers in
359	use, a failed pull, an old image that could not be removed).
360	
361	**On a narrow terminal**, the containers table drops the two gauges before
362	Update (they are `DropFirst`, §3.71), then the I/O counters, then Update. Both
363	gauges now need 180 columns instead of 160.
364	
365	**Not done**: a digest for a tag the engine holds under another name, and the
366	`podman` side of `RepoDigests` has not been measured against a real `podman
367	system service` — the field exists there under the same name.
368	
369	**From a container to its image — `J`** (§3.89). The containers view sends
370	`ociresources.FocusImageRequestMsg` with the image reference exactly as the
371	engine printed it; the router switches to the OCI view and hands it the
372	request, which waits for the first listing if the view was just built
373	(`deferUntilListed`, the same queue agents use). Matching is the OCI view's
374	(`imageMatches`, `focus.go`): an implicit `latest`, docker's `nginx` against
375	podman's `docker.io/library/nginx`, a registry port that is not a tag, a
376	`repo@sha256:` digest against `RepoDigests`, and a bare ID — what `ps` shows
377	once the tag has moved to a newer image. A search hiding the target is
378	dropped; an image that is no longer listed is a footer `Warn`. There is no
379	`esc` back: `:ct` returns, as from any other view.

381	## The OCI tables and the activity column — `internal/ui/oci_resources` (DEVDESK-146, A-09a; DEVDESK-153, A-09b)
382	
383	The four tables of `:oci` (Images, Networks, Volumes, Registries) and the
384	registry browser's tag table are on the activity column (Rule 125; the router
385	side is in `app-shell.md`).
386	
387	**Periodic refresh and terminal focus (DEVDESK-210).** `refreshInterval` is 10 s
388	(a var, so a test can shorten it). `RefreshTickMsg` used to refresh once and
389	never again; it now re-arms `tickCmd()` on every tick. While `Model.blurred` is
390	set (from `shared.TerminalFocusMsg`) the tick only re-arms and skips
391	`refreshReads()` (images, scan cache, networks, volumes; it never scans, Rule
392	126). On the focus edge (`Resume`) it runs `refreshReads()` once, with no new tick.
393	
394	**Registry browser (DEVDESK-218, A-09a2).** The tag table
395	(`registry_browser.go`, built by `newTagTable`, which `ActivityTables` also uses
396	so the guard sees the real table open or not, as `oci/registry-browser`) takes
397	`datatable.IndicatorColumn` as column 0, an 8th column; Registry, Tag and
398	Updated are 1 to 3 (`tagColumnTag` = 2, `tagColumnUpdated` = 3). `tagRow` holds
399	`Activity components.RowActivity` and `ScanRunning`, stamped by
400	`rebuildTagTable` from `components.DescribeRow` (scan and pull, `ociKinds`,
401	target `jobs.TargetKey(imageName)`) over the snapshot the router pushes through
402	`SetJobs(runs, failures, context)`; the cell at rest is empty. While a scan
403	really runs (not queued) the C/H/M/L cells hold `…` in `DimStyle`; a queued scan
404	or a pull keeps the counts. The blink phase arrives with `SetBlinkPhase` and
405	`WantsBlink` is true for a visible running tag row. Rule 116: Updated drops
406	under 102 columns, L under 84, M under 78, H under 72, C under 66; at 60 only
407	the dot, Registry and Tag remain. The browser has no spinner of its own
408	(DEVDESK-374): a search shows the shared activity dot in the footer
409	(`Searching registries...`), and `WantsBlink` is true while it runs. After the search the
410	footer describes the selected tag (`Status{Detail}`). `tagScanSpinnerIdx` and
411	the local frame are deleted. `DescribeRow` filters by context: a scan of another
412	context no longer shows on a tag (D108).
413	
414	**Cancelling a lot and ignoring late answers (DEVDESK-298, IS-18).** The
415	browser launches requests in lots (one per validation that starts something).
416	`browserGen` is a package-wide `atomic.Uint64`, incremented only from `Update`
417	(`nextBrowserGen`). `beginRequests()` cancels the previous lot (one
418	`CancelFunc`, `cancelRequests`, per lot, not per registry), takes a new
419	generation and resets `pendingSearches`; the `context` is born in `Update`
420	(Rule 110). `MultiRegistryTagsLoadedMsg`, `MultiRegistryTagsMetaMsg` and
421	`ImageSearchResultMsg` carry the `Gen` they were started with, and their
422	handlers return before logging anything when it differs from the open
423	browser's. The counter is global rather than per browser so that a browser
424	closed and reopened, or a new `Model` after a context switch, cannot accept the
425	answer of an older instance. `closeMultiRegistryBrowser` calls
426	`cancelInFlight()`, which also covers closing through `G` (a pull). A validation
427	that starts nothing (empty name, no registry checked) cancels nothing and
428	leaves `gen` alone. The tag lookups go through the `listRegistryTags` variable
429	(`oci.ListRegistryTagsContext`), the seam tests swap to capture the context;
430	there is no deadline on a tag lookup, only `maxTagPages` and the per-request
431	client timeout. `Model.RegistryBrowserGen()` exposes the generation to tests
432	only.
433	
434	**Level 1: image search (DEVDESK-299, IS-01; Open Tags DEVDESK-300, IS-11).**
435	The browser has three states: `browserStateInput` (form), `browserStateImages`
436	(level 1, appended last in the `iota` list) and `browserStateTags` (level 2).
437	
438	*The form's buttons.* `formButtons()` (`browser_form.go`) is the single source
439	of the buttons: the keyboard, the rendering (`renderFormButtons`, one line) and
440	the header (`FormEnter`) all read it. Without a `Searcher` there is one button,
441	`Browse Tags` (action `actionSearch`). With one there are two, `Search`
442	(`actionSearch`) then `Open Tags` (`actionOpenTags`).
443	
444	*Field indices.* Repository is `brFieldRepo` (0); the picker checkboxes are
445	1..n (n = `len(b.rows)`); the buttons follow: `brFieldButton(i)` = `1 + n + i`,

449	*Validation.* `submit(action)` is common to both actions: an empty name starts
450	nothing; no registry checked sends `RegistryBrowserWarnMsg{"No registry
451	selected"}`, which the `Model` shows as a footer warning (the browser has no
452	footer; this also applies to a name that contains `/`, where the tag flow used
453	to refuse silently). Then `actionOpenTags` always goes to `startTagLookup`

455	IS-01 rule: a name with no `/` goes to `startImageSearch` when `b.searcher !=
456	nil`, anything else to `startTagLookup`. `enter` on Repository runs
457	`actionSearch`; `enter` on a button runs that button's action; `enter` on a
458	checkbox only advances the focus. The selection applies to both actions.
459	
460	*Header.* `FormEnter()` returns the label and the lit state of the header's
461	single `enter` entry. The label follows the focus: `Search` on Repository and
462	on the Search button (`Browse tags` without a `Searcher`), `Open tags` on the
463	Open Tags button. `enter` is lit on Repository (Rule 130: it submits there) and
464	on a button, and greyed on a checkbox.
465	
466	*Help.* `registryBrowserHelpBody(searchEnabled)` (`view.go`) depends on the
467	mode (Rule 114): without a `Searcher` it names Browse Tags only; with one it

470	**`defaultImageSearcher` is `ByRegistry(HubSearcher{}, CatalogSearcher{})` in
471	production (DEVDESK-301, IS-02; catalog since DEVDESK-306, IS-03), so level 1

477	`TestProductionWiresTheHubSearcher` reads the saved value. `internal/app`

480	`startImageSearch` runs one `searchImagesCmd` per checked registry, with
481	`targetFor(entry)` (same credentials as the tag flow, `credsFor`). Each command
482	wraps the lot's context in `context.WithTimeout(ctx, imageSearchDeadline)`:

489	**Verdicts per registry (DEVDESK-303, IS-12).** `AddImageResults` calls
490	`imagesearch.Classify` in `Update`, never in the `Cmd` (Rule 110), and stores the
491	result in `RegistryBrowser.outcomes`, keyed by `EntryKey`. The map is reset by

497	**Level 1 header summary (DEVDESK-305, IS-13).** `searchHeaderInfo`
498	(`browser_summary.go`, called from `GetHeaderInfo`) says what the lot did, one
499	header line per class, in this order: `Images` (the row count, always), then
500	`Pending` (a count, live lot) or `Interrupted` (names, the lot was abandoned
501	with the left arrow before they answered), `Failed` (red), `Refused`, `Partial`
502	(orange), `Cached only` (orange, DEVDESK-308, IS-14), `No result` (dim) and `Skipped` (dim, catalog not walked because the
503	query is shorter than `imagesearch.CatalogMinQueryRunes`). A class with nothing

505	`summarizeSearch` (pure) sorts the lot's keys into the classes. A name is the
506	Registry column's label (`entryLabel`: alias, else URL, else key), in form order.
507	`Partial` lists registries cut at a cap, `No result` those that answered with

509	on both lines, on purpose.

511	`Cached only` lists the registries whose list is limited to cached content: a
512	`provider: nexus` + `kind: group` entry, or a member of such a group (a
513	discovered member, or a declared entry whose `parent` is the slug of one).
514	`config.IsNexusGroup` and `listsCacheOnly` decide, once, into

522	group never get the line. `Cached only` and `Skipped` exclude each other, which
523	keeps the budget below. Nexus's cache-only behavior comes from secondary
524	sources and is not verified on a real Nexus (to confirm in IS-16).

531	included; classes after the sixth are left out (with `Cached only` the seven

537	Limit, accepted (R2): below about 50 columns `HeaderValueWidth` is 0 or 1,
